accuracy.evidence: 608 checked against NC Year 3 forces and magnets statutory text (two poles; attract or repel depending on which poles face) and NGSS 3-PS2-3. Facts verified: free magnet's north-seeking pole points north; like repel/unlike attract for all four pairings; field strongest at poles; snapped magnet gives two complete magnets; attraction alone does not prove magnetism because iron is attracted, repulsion does.

misconceptions.evidence: Targets documented primary misconceptions about magnets: like poles attract (Ben item, N–N prediction), S–S behaving differently from N–N (table prediction), strongest pull in the middle (clips), one pole per broken piece, poles as + and − charges (adult text), and 'it was pulled so it is a magnet' (mystery step, m5, m7).

lab_distinct.evidence: flagpoles models pole interactions: pivoting magnet settling north, drag that snaps for unlike poles and springs back for like poles, a 4-row results table and a repulsion test on an unlabelled bar. flagmag (512) only sorts which materials a magnet pulls; lab gate measured shingle overlap under 30% with every flag_*.js.

lab_teaches.evidence: The learner feels the rule before it is stated: dragging S to N snaps, N to N springs back, then flipping magnets fills the table so 'same push, different pull' is read off their own results; clips show where the pull is strongest; the mystery step makes them apply repulsion as the decisive test.

predictions.evidence: Five predictions, each with a tempting wrong option the lab then disproves: 'any way at all' for a free magnet, 'push apart' for S–N, 'pull together' for N–N (the 'matching sticks' idea), 'pull together' for S–S, and 'in the middle' for the clips.

challenge_feedback.evidence: Seven challenge items with distinct messages for each slip: unlike-poles-push, same-poles-pull, 'nothing happens', middle/same strength, south/any direction for a compass, pull-as-proof, and one-pole/no-pole after snapping.

readability.evidence: Kid text uses short sentences with the precise Year 3 terms (pole, north pole, south pole, attract, repel, like and unlike poles) each explained in plain words; validator FK check passes the family kid and adult targets; lab lines are one short sentence.

no_filler.evidence: Content gate found no filler phrases; every kid paragraph states one fact (two poles, pointing north, attract, repel, strongest at poles) and the adult text gives the standard, the reason for the names, named mistakes and what the lab does.

mobile.evidence: Checked iPhone 13 screenshots in dark and light for all 7 steps: magnets, N/S letters and the results table are readable, young 56 px buttons sit under the canvas, nothing clipped; drag uses pointer capture with touch-action none on the canvas.

accessibility.evidence: Every drag has a button twin (Spin and let go, Move closer, Flip left/right, Push together, Dip N end/middle/S end, Test end A/B, A is N/B is N); canvas aria-label is updated with each result; walk.cjs axe clean in both themes on desktop and iPhone 13.
